conviction_note: Net of a genuinely favourable rate-regime flip (+3.0) against three separate negatives that all land inside the quarter actually being reported (-6.0), I get -3.0; I kept it small because the baseline has no option chain and therefore no statement of what the market priced, and because a +8.97% five-day run-up may already be the rate trade I am counting as my one positive.

findings.finding: Wealthfront's annualized cash management fee rate is running below its own guide and still falling — the company guided ~0.59% for fiscal Q1 2027, printed 0.58%, and the CFO disclosed on the 2026-06-04 call that the May-end rate was 54 basis points; the cause is the 'Direct Deposit + Investing' +0.25% APY boost launched 2026-03-02 which carries no expiration and no balance cap, so it compounds mechanically as asset-weighted cross-product adoption rises (61% at FY26 year-end, 62.5% at April, over 63% at June).
findings.why_not_priced: The 54bp datapoint was disclosed, but its structure was not: an uncapped, non-expiring giveaway indexed to a KPI management is actively promoting means the spread falls further every month adoption rises, which is the opposite of a one-off reset. If the street had modelled that, the July target cuts would not have landed at roughly spot ($10 revised target vs $9.66 close) and the 6-analyst consensus would not still read Buy at a $12.25 average. At $44.8bn of cash assets each 1bp is ~$4.5m of annual revenue, so 54bp to 51bp is ~$13m/yr against a company that lost $42.1m in FY26.
findings.independence: The +0.25% no-expiration, no-balance-cap structure is confirmed independently on Wealthfront's own live pricing page (https://www.wealthfront.com/cash, base APY 3.30% as of 01/30/2026, '+0.25% APY increase—no expiration date or balance limit'), which is a different source from the earnings call. The cross-product adoption series comes from a third source, the June monthly metrics release (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/07/3323635/0/en/wealthfront-reports-june-2026-monthly-metrics.html).

findings.finding: Fiscal Q2 2027 is a structurally mismatched quarter: it covers 2026-05-01 to 2026-07-31, during which the Fed did not move (held 3.50-3.75% on 2026-07-29, unchanged since December 2025) so no rate benefit accrued, while Wealthfront Home Lending only launched in California and Texas on 2026-08-11 — after quarter end — meaning the full pre-launch mortgage build cost sits in Q2 with essentially zero mortgage revenue, on top of Q1 GAAP expenses already up 46% year-over-year to $75.9m against 7% revenue growth.
findings.why_not_priced: Coverage of the 2026-08-11 launch was uniformly framed as a growth event ('rates ~0.50% below the national average', expansion to FL/IL/OR/WA), not as a calendar problem for the quarter reporting three weeks later. A market that had done the date arithmetic would not have marked the stock up 8.97% in the five sessions into a print whose expense line carries a launch it cannot yet monetise; the run-up looks like a growth read, not a cost read. Wealthfront's 10-K states home lending revenue was immaterial in FY2026, so there is no offsetting revenue base.
findings.independence: The 46% expense growth and the 'startup expenses tied to Wealthfront Home Lending' attribution come from the same 2026-06-04 call cited in finding 1 — that overlap is real and this finding should not be double-counted with it. The independent leg is the launch date itself (2026-08-11 vs a 2026-07-31 quarter end) plus Wealthfront's own careers page still carrying three unfilled Mortgage Operations roles as of today (https://www.wealthfront.com/careers), i.e. the cost ramp is ongoing, not complete.

findings.finding: Schwab disclosed on 2026-08-14 that transactional sweep cash fell $8.9bn in July 2026 to $476.8bn — 1.8% of the balance in one month — 'reflecting client net purchasing activity as well as typical seasonality related to advisory fee payments', and the S&P 500 then rose 2.7% in August to record highs; at Wealthfront a dollar migrating from cash to investing loses roughly 60% of its revenue (cash fee rate ~54bp vs investment advisory running ~21bp annualised on $26.2m of quarterly revenue against ~$50bn of advisory assets), so the same client behaviour that will produce a record platform-assets headline tonight is revenue-dilutive.
findings.why_not_priced: Wealthfront publishes monthly metrics only for months one and two of each fiscal quarter — the last public flow datapoint is June, released 2026-07-07 (Cash Management Net Deposits -$235m). July and August flows are both released for the first time tonight. No WLTH-specific wire item connects Schwab's July sweep decline to Wealthfront's undisclosed July cash flow; if that link were priced you would see WLTH coverage referencing it and the stock would not be flat over 20 days while its cash-heavy revenue mix was being drained. Sized small and with a wide band because the read-across is genuinely ambiguous: June's -$235m is partly the 15 June estimated-tax date, and the S&P fell in both June and July, which normally favours cash.
findings.independence: Wealthfront's own June metrics show cash management assets already shrinking year-over-year (-2.1%, $44.8bn vs $45.7bn) with net deposits at -$235m: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/07/3323635/0/en/wealthfront-reports-june-2026-monthly-metrics.html. The August equity rally to record highs is a third source: https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/04/investing/us-stock-market.

findings.finding: The rate regime that defines this company's entire bear case has flipped: the FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% on 2026-07-29 with three regional presidents dissenting in favour of a 25bp HIKE, and futures price roughly 60% odds of a hike at the 2026-09-16 meeting one week after this print — while Wealthfront has held its base Cash Account APY at 3.30% since 2026-01-30 and its own 10-K states that 'in weaker macroeconomic environments with higher interest rates, our cash management products become more popular.'
findings.why_not_priced: Every plaintiff-firm investigation opened on this name (BFA 2026-03-16, Pomerantz 2026-07-07, Robbins and Johnson Fistel 2026-08-20) alleges misstatements about 'interest rate sensitivity' and asset flows — the whole public narrative is that falling rates break the model. A price that had absorbed a live hike would not sit 31% below the $14 December 2025 IPO price and 30.8% below its 52-week high with the S&P at record highs. Management is near-certain to be asked to quantify hike sensitivity on a call held eight days before the FOMC, and has an unusually good answer for the first time since listing. I have discounted this from a larger number because the +8.97% five-day run-up, into the week of a strong August payroll print, is plausibly this trade already starting.
findings.independence: Wealthfront's own live pricing page independently confirms the APY has not moved since 01/30/2026, so a hike would accrue almost entirely to the spread rather than to clients: https://www.wealthfront.com/cash. The 10-K's own framing of higher rates as good for the cash business is a second, company-sourced leg: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001524566/000162828026027232/wlth-20260131.htm.

findings.finding: Tonight is a double-disclosure event, not a normal print: because Wealthfront publishes monthly metrics only for the first two months of each fiscal quarter, the 2026-08-19 scheduling release states that metrics 'through August 2026' will be posted with the results — meaning July (fiscal Q2's third month) and August (fiscal Q3's first month) flows both become public for the first time tonight, alongside the P&L.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a variance finding, not a directional one, and I have given it zero expected impact deliberately. It matters because the baseline's option chain is unusable (609 total open interest, ATM bid-ask 127% of mid) so there is no priced statement of magnitude at all, and the only anchor is a three-event history of -16.84%, -6.19% and -14.35%. Two months of unseen flow data plus a quarter of P&L is exactly why this name's prints move double digits, and it argues the realised move will be at the wide end regardless of sign.
findings.independence: Confirmed by the absence of any July or August monthly metrics release on Wealthfront's own press index, which lists only 2026-07-07 (June metrics), 2026-08-11 (home lending) and 2026-08-19 between June and today: https://press.wealthfront.com/.

searched_and_found_nothing: Insider activity: the 2026-08-19 Form 4 is CTO Julien Wetterwald selling 15,263 shares under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-01-14, and the 2026-08-26 Form 4 is a routine 207,000 RSU grant to CLO/CCO Lauren Lin vesting from 2026-12-15 — no discretionary cluster, nothing to read.

Securities litigation: four plaintiff firms are 'investigating' (BFA, Pomerantz, Robbins, Johnson Fistel) but Rosen's case page shows no active case and BFA's case list does not carry Wealthfront, so no complaint has been filed and there is no new legal-proceedings footnote to anticipate.

Promotional escalation as a distress tell: the new-client +0.65%/3-month boost and +0.75% referral boost on wealthfront.com/cash are unchanged from the 2026-01-29 blog description, and the base APY is still 3.30% as of 01/30/2026 — no sign of a panic bid for deposits in July or August.
Wayback Machine has no captures of wealthfront.com/cash around 2026-08-15, so I could not build an APY time series independent of the company's own 'as of' dates.
Careers page is unremarkable: 31 open roles, three in Home Lending, two AML/compliance analysts — no team deleted, no hiring freeze, no surprise new function.
Customer-complaint channels (BBB F rating on 32 unanswered complaints, ConsumerAffairs, teamblind) show generic transfer-delay and support gripes with no dated spike tied to July or August.
Form ADV Part 1 on IAPD as an independent AUM read: updates annually in March, so it offers no datapoint between the June and September prints.

IPO lock-up: the December 2025 IPO's 180-day lock-up expired in mid-June 2026, which the 2026-06-15/17/22/25 Form 144 and Form 4 cluster confirms — that supply event is behind the stock, not ahead of it.

Could not retrieve Item 3 of the 2026-06-12 10-Q (the fetcher truncated the document), so I have no company-quantified basis-point rate sensitivity; the 10-K contains no quantified sensitivity table either.
baseline_tension: There is no skew and no straddle to agree or disagree with — the chain carries 609 contracts of open interest and a 127%-of-mid ATM spread, so the baseline's 14.35% 'expected move' is only the median of three prior reactions and tells me nothing about what was priced, which is the single biggest reason I am at -3.0 rather than a larger number; my net cuts with the 0-for-3 down reaction history but against the +8.97% five-day run-up, and the one positive I found (a live September hike) is the most plausible explanation for that run-up, so I have deliberately not counted it twice.
